title: cost-optimization-autotune-batching-caching-quant-uecon-tooling
author: Maya Patel
description: Motivation: Customers run a wide range of workloads and we continue to see substantial unit-cost variance due to suboptimal batching, cache defaults, and quantization choices. This PR adds an end-to-end autotune and defaults framework to make safer cost-optimization suggestions and to apply recommended defaults automatically for controlled cohorts. It also ships Unit Economics (UEcon) tooling in the console and a small CLI for operators to inspect per-route token economics. Scope summary: 1) runtime: new 'autotune' controller that observes latency, throughput, and unit-cost signals to recommend batching/caching defaults and quant profiles; 2) model profiles: bundled quantization profile presets (int8/int4 mixed) for common model families + compatibility matrix; 3) console + CLI: new UEcon dashboard panels and a CLI command `redwood uecon inspect` that shows per-route cost breakdown and recommended profile; 4) safety: rollout controller for canarying default changes with automatic rollback on quality regressions; 5) tests & CI: unit, integration, and perf harness runs added to pipeline. This description includes motivation, implementation notes, and rollout considerations.
commits: a) Add autotune controller (autotune/controller.go + tests) b) Bundle quant profiles (model/profiles/*.json) c) Add UEcon instrumentation (observability/uecon_metrics.go) d) Console panels and API endpoints (console/uecon/*) e) CLI command (cli/uecon.go) f) E2E perf job and CI matrix update (ci/perf.yml) g) Documentation updates (docs/uecon.md) — commit messages are focused and small; tests added for controller heuristics and perf regressions.
files_changed_summary: 1) runtime/autotune/controller.go — new controller implementing observation window, scoring, and recommendation API. 2) model/profiles/quant-presets.json — bundled presets for gpt-like and llama-like families (int8, int4-mix). 3) serving/batching/defaults.go — plumb in recommended batch/window defaults and expose override hooks. 4) serving/caching/prefix_cache.go — added metrics hooks and TTL tuning to support dynamic defaults. 5) console/server/uecon_routes.go & console/ui/uecon.html — new UEcon dashboard and per-route views. 6) cli/uecon.go — `redwood uecon inspect <route>` command that shows tokens, cost, and recommended profile. 7) ci/perf.yml — new perf job that runs autotune smoke tests on PRs labeled perf. 8) docs/uecon.md — how to interpret recommendations and rollout safely. Small code snippets: in controller.go added scoring: "score = 0.6*latency_impact + 0.3*cost_savings + 0.1*quality_delta".
review_comments: Liam Chen: Please add more detail about how quality_delta is computed and thresholds for rollback. Maya: quality_delta is a rolling A/B evaluation metric computed from our eval-harness using the canonical prompt set for the route; added details and tests in tests/autotune/quality_test.go. Aria Gomez: Concerns about canary rollout cadence and number of users in canary. Maya: implemented configurable canary size and a default conservative cadence (5% -> 25% -> 100%) with automatic rollback if quality_delta > 1% or latency SLO is violated; documented in docs/uecon.md. Ravi Narayan: CI perf job adds notable time to pipeline; can we gate on label? Maya: perf job is gated on label `perf` and runs in parallel on a separate runner; added note to ci/perf.yml. Final review: approvals from Liam and Aria after small nits addressed; Ravi approved after CI green and perf gating confirmed. Merge maintainer comment: Squashed and merged; kept individual commits in changelog.
release_notes: Adds an autotune controller to recommend and apply safe batching/caching defaults and quantization profiles. Bundles quant presets for common model families. Introduces UEcon dashboard and CLI tooling for per-route unit economics. Rollouts are canaried with automatic rollback on quality or latency regressions. Opt-in perf CI job added (label: perf).
additional_notes: Rollout plan: start with internal beta (10 routes), monitor UEcon panels for 2 weeks, then expand. Operators can opt-out per-route. Follow-up work: 1) ML-based scoring for quality_delta; 2) more quant profiles for custom architectures; 3) telemetry to correlate cache hit ratios with cost impact.
examples_and_screenshots: Console UEcon panel shows per-route TPS, avg latency, tokens per request, cost per 1k tokens, recommended quant profile, and projected monthly savings. CLI sample: `redwood uecon inspect /chat/completions` -> shows current profile: fp16, recommendation: int8-mix-v2, est savings: 22%/token, confidence: high.
test_plan: Unit tests for scoring and threshold logic, integration tests for applying recommendations to a local serving stack, perf harness runs comparing baseline vs recommended profiles (latency, throughput, token-cost), and manual QA of console panels. CI matrix updated to include autotune unit tests and gated perf job.
risk_and_mitigation: Risk: quality regressions from aggressive quantization or batching. Mitigation: conservative default thresholds, canary rollouts, automatic rollback on quality/latency thresholds, and an operator override. Added extensive automated A/B checks in eval-harness.
notes_for_release_engineering: This change touches model bundles and console schema. Release engineers should ensure model/profiles/* are uploaded to artifact store and console migrations run. DB migration: new table `uecon_recommendations` added (migration script included). Backwards compatibility: recommendations are opt-in per route until the cohort expansion job runs.
